title: Prompt-conditioned continuation on a toy model
goal:
VALL-E never updates its weights for a new speaker. The 3-second acoustic prompt sits in the context and the model continues it in the same voice (Section 4.3). This exercise builds the smallest model that shows the effect: a Bayesian mixture over $K$ "speakers", each a first-order Markov chain over $V$ tokens with transition matrix `trans[k]`.

Write `speaker_posterior(prompt, trans, prior)`, the posterior over speakers given the prompt, which is $p(k \mid \text{prompt}) \propto p(k) \prod_{t} \text{trans}[k, \text{prompt}_t, \text{prompt}_{t+1}]$. Write `next_token_dist(prefix, trans, prior)`, the mixture $\sum_k p(k \mid \text{prefix})\, \text{trans}[k, \text{prefix}_{-1}, \cdot]$. Write `continue_greedy(prefix, n, trans, prior)`, which appends $n$ arg-max tokens and returns the whole list. This toy is not VALL-E's computation. It is the behavior that VALL-E has to learn implicitly.
hints: Work in log space. Add `np.log(trans[:, a, b])` for each adjacent pair, then subtract the maximum before `np.exp`.
A prompt with one token has no transitions, so the posterior is the prior.
In `continue_greedy`, recompute the next-token distribution from the grown prefix on every step, because each new token is more evidence about the speaker.
